Thus $B'$ has nonplanar triangle completion. Contracting
$\operatorname{Int}(B)$ keeps $H$ nonplanar, so the same criterion
and minimality make $\operatorname{Int}(B)$ a single vertex.
A $b$--$d$ path with interior in $\operatorname{Int}(B)$ shows
that the triangle completion of $B'$ is a minor of $H$, so it
contains a $K_{3,3}$ subdivision.
An allowed reduction of $B'$ keeping this subdivision keeps $H$
nonplanar and would again give a proper nontoroidal minor.
Thus Lemma~\ref{core:retained-subdivision} and
Construction~\ref{common:marked-construction}, with attachments
$a,b,d$ and the added triangle, give every possible $B'$.
The $216$ forms, with $bd$ absent or present, give $432$ graphs.
Each has a $K_5$ minor, a cut of at most two vertices, or a proper
nontoroidal minor~\supp{E21}.

vertex names: Psi_3: twins p, q with neighbourhood {a,b,c} and r, z with neighbourhood {a,d,e}, as in Section 6. Further vertices with neighbourhood {a,b,c} are p3, p4, and with {a,d,e} r3, r4. Interior vertices of bridges are u0, u1, ...
